21281.title: [Core] Minimize number of dict lookup in _maybe_evict_cached_block (#21281)

experiments.name: allocate_new_block
experiments.note: runs = per allocate-block size, median of 3 reps; speedup = mean of per-size base/gold ratios

reported.scope: per-call TRACE of allocate_new_block, measured on top of PR #21222
reported.scale_note: WORKLOAD INVALID (measured 1.007x is meaningless, do not trust). The PR cuts 4->2 dict lookups of the same key in _maybe_evict_cached_block, but that body ONLY runs when block_hash is not None AND block_hash in cached_block_hash_to_block (a cached block being evicted). Our benchmark_block_pool sweep pulls free blocks with block_hash=None, so BOTH arms hit the membership-fail early-out and the 4->2 reduction never executes. FIX NEEDED: enable_caching=True; assign each test block a non-None block_hash; pre-populate cached_block_hash_to_block[block_hash]={block_id:block} so the membership HITS; loop _maybe_evict_cached_block on those cached blocks (re-insert each iter). Only then does base pay 4 same-key hashes vs gold's 2 -> expect ~2x isolated (author's 4.3x is a profiler trace delta on top of #21222, an upper bound incl. surrounding overhead). Author number 0.13->0.03ms published as prose, no input sizes.

27793.note: OBSERVABILITY FEATURE, not a perf optimization. Title: '[Core][Observability] Add KV cache residency metrics'. Adds 3 Prometheus histograms (kv_block_lifetime/idle_before_evict/reuse_gap) behind --kv-cache-metrics flags (default 1% sampling) via new KVCacheMetricsCollector in block_pool hot paths (on_block_allocated/accessed/evicted), each guarded by `if self.metrics_collector:` so disabled=zero cost. 29499.title: [EPLB] Optimize EPLB with numpy (#29499)

experiments.name: move_from_buffer
experiments.workload: per-rank mapping over 16 local experts (2048-slot cluster); 5 repeats x best-of-100
experiments.note: inline-from-diff: exact duplicate-resolution mapping body copied verbatim from base_sha / merge_sha (tensor .copy_ excluded as arm-identical). per-rank body over num_local_experts=16 rows; numpy overhead dominates at this size so gold is slower. unit ms/op. speedup = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios

reported.scale_note: NOT CPU-REPRODUCIBLE. Headline is end-to-end rearrange 1370->1077ms (~27%); this primitive is in the separate '20-25% per primitive' claim (pct~0.225), no absolute ms pair. PRECISE mechanism: the numpy rewrite moved only the INDEX/MASK bookkeeping (np.isin/unique/lexsort/searchsorted) off GPU tensors; the tensor .copy_(non_blocking=True) transfers themselves are UNCHANGED across arms. Author's #1 bullet 'removes multiple gpu-cpu transfers in move_from_buffer' + preserve_intragpu_slots avoids memcopies -- a GPU-sync/transfer saving invisible on CPU. On CPU-only our microbench pays the numpy bookkeeping overhead with NO GPU-sync elision to offset it -> gold SLOWER (0.245x). Sub-1x contradicts no published number (author ran no CPU microbench); real gain is on the GPU path.

experiments.name: get_ep_ranks_with_expert
experiments.workload: 128 ranks x 16 local = 2048 physical slots, 256 logical experts; 5 repeats x best-of-100
experiments.note: isolated import of real function from each tree. base loops get_ep_ranks_with_expert over all unique experts; gold makes one get_ep_ranks_with_experts_batch call. unit ms/op (whole-layer rank-map computation). speedup = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios

reported.scale_note: PR gives '20-25% on average for each primitive' (pct~0.225), no absolute pair. This is the ONE primitive that is pure-CPU and genuinely batchable: base loops get_ep_ranks_with_expert per-expert, gold does one batched call -> our 8.3x is a real CPU-reproducible win whose DIRECTION agrees with the PR, but the magnitude is not 1:1 with the PR's 20-25% because the PR's percent is diluted across the whole EPLB step (including GPU-transfer primitives). Absolute ms not comparable (no reported pair).

experiments.name: move_to_buffer
experiments.workload: per-rank mapping over 16 local experts (2048-slot cluster); 5 repeats x best-of-100
experiments.note: inline-from-diff: exact index-mapping body copied verbatim from base_sha / merge_sha (P2P + .copy_ excluded as arm-identical). per-rank body over num_local_experts=16 rows; numpy overhead dominates at this size so gold is slower. unit ms/op. speedup = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios

reported.scale_note: GPU-TRANSFER-BOUND, NOT CPU-REPRODUCIBLE. Same as move_from_buffer: PR's '20-25% per primitive' (pct~0.225) is dominated by eliding GPU P2P + tensor .copy_ round-trips (arm-identical, excluded). The residual numpy index-mapping body over 16 local experts is too small for numpy to win -> gold SLOWER (0.659x) on CPU. 32975.title: [Perf] Optimize detokenizer python logic (#32975)

experiments.name: detokenize
experiments.workload: 200 seqs x 2000 tokens; isolated SlowIncrementalDetokenizer per-token output-count check (slice vs tracked), 7 repeats
experiments.note: approach=fallback (self-contained, both arms in ONE process on the same CPU, no cross-container noise). Reproduces the exact changed inner logic: base recomputes len(self.token_ids[self.prompt_len:]) per token (slice alloc), gold uses num_output_tokens()==len(token_ids)-prompt_len. speedup_x = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios. NOTE: the real full detokenizer path was ALSO driven (PYTHONPATH=/src, real gpt2 tokenizer via transformers, real SlowIncrementalDetokenizer.update() loop, batched updates, long prompt); there the native tokenizer decode (~5us/tok) dominates and the slice removal is below run-to-run noise (real base ~5.36 us/tok vs gold ~6.39 us/tok, i.e. no measurable end-to-end gain). The isolated fallback below matches the PR's own reported methodology of timing the detokenizer PYTHON logic in isolation.

reported.scope: benchmark_detokenizer_min_tokens.py: 39.36 ns/token -> 24.18 ns/token (1.628x, -38.57%) -- but this benchmarks the min_tokens offset-accumulation loop that was REVERTED, not the merged change
reported.scale_note: UNIT-BUG FIXED + SCOPE CAVEAT. Earlier this field held base=1.628/patch=1.0, pasting the SPEEDUP RATIO as an absolute us/tok value; real PR numbers are 39.36->24.18 ns/token = 0.03936->0.02418 us/tok. BUT the 1.628x is unrepresentative TWICE OVER: (1) the PR's benchmark_detokenizer_min_tokens.py times a synthetic pure-Python int/str accumulation loop (new_chars_len += len(piece) vs stop_check_offset += len(piece)) with NO tokenizer / NO update() / NO slice -- it measures the min_tokens stop_check_offset change, which was REVERTED (njhill 2026-02-06; only num_output_tokens was merged). (2) njhill noted the common case is 1 token/update where the change is MORE work, so the benchmark doesn't reflect production. Our microbench isolates the actually-merged num_output_tokens() slice-vs-count primitive (base ~1.33 us/tok, 11x). Direction agrees; the PR's 1.628x and our 11x measure different code and are not comparable.

33593.title: [Perf] Optimize Python Slice for Structured Output using `islice` instead of [:] (#33593)

experiments.name: membership_present
experiments.workload: SIZE=100_000, end-token at 10%% in; `tok not in input_ids[:-1]` vs `tok not in islice(input_ids,0,len-1)`; INNER=200 calls/block, 18 paired samples, best-of + mean±sd
experiments.note: Real PR hot path (reasoning parser extract_content_ids). Marker present early -> islice short-circuits + copies nothing; list[:-1] copies all N first. Gold wins.

reported.scope: PR microbench 'create slice' on a 2,000,000-element list, N=1,000,000: list[:N] 0.003368s vs islice 0.000001s (materialization cost, NOT a membership test)
reported.scale_note: DIFFERENT EXPERIMENT: the PR's 0.0034->1e-6 is pure list[:N] MATERIALIZATION (allocating the copy). Our membership_present measures the REAL hot-path idiom `tok not in islice(...)` which short-circuits -- a different operation. 3400x (the PR's alloc elision) is not the same quantity as our 2.31x (short-circuit membership). Honest: we measure the actual call site, the PR measured the underlying primitive in isolation.

experiments.name: membership_absent
experiments.workload: SIZE=100_000, end-token absent; same two idioms; INNER=200, 18 paired samples
experiments.note: HONEST TRADEOFF: when the token is absent both scan all N, but list[:-1] is a C-level memcpy + C-level `in`, while islice yields through the Python iterator protocol per element. Gold is SLOWER here. Net PR win depends on how often reasoning has already ended (present case dominates in practice).

reported.scale_note: CONSUMER DIFFERS. The PR's absent-case number comes from summing/materializing the whole slice (list[:-1] then consume all N); our membership_absent scans for a token that never occurs. Both are O(N) but list[:-1] is a C-level memcpy + C `in`, while islice yields per-element through the Python iterator protocol -> gold is SLOWER here (our 0.78x vs the PR's ~1.18x). Sign flips because the operation after the slice is not the same primitive. This is the honest tradeoff case: islice only wins when the marker is present (short-circuit), which dominates in practice.

experiments.name: cache_lookup
experiments.workload: InductorPass.hash_source repeated over 5 source objects, 10000 lookups/repeat, 5 repeats; per-call ms
experiments.note: base = recompute inspect.getsource+sha256 each call; gold = functools.cache wrapped (cold miss then hits); speedup = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios

reported.scope: ms per 'cache lookup' (PR body does not define granularity; likely per-uuid() computation -- inferred, not quoted)
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (ms) but NOT scale-comparable. Reported 32.5->11.3ms is the PR's 'cache lookup time' whose scope the PR body does NOT specify (inferred to be per full uuid() computation over the pass classes).
